_what: THE REFRESH LOG. Current-state timestamps for every registered data poll. Routine Ricky TRIAGES this on a bare invocation (reads it, computes what is due against each poll's cadence, and PROPOSES a refresh). Procedure: hooks/data-refresh.md. Renderer: none yet.
_config_vs_state: ⚠️ THE SPLIT THAT KEEPS THIS HONEST. This file holds STATE ONLY (when did it last run, what happened). The SCHEDULE — each poll's `cadence`, its pinned sources, whether it is in the default sweep — is CONFIG and lives in the poll registry in hooks/data-refresh.md. Never duplicate cadence here: two claimants on one truth is the rot that killed registry.json and the old app-index. If a row here disagrees with the registry, the registry wins for cadence and this file wins for timestamps.
_anyone_may_stamp: NOT Ricky's private file. ANY agent (or Michael) who actually refreshes a poll stamps it here — that is the whole point: the schedule is externally maintained and Ricky reads shared state rather than his own memory. A fact about when work happened belongs on the shared record, never in one agent's head (memory-first). Ricky's own memory.md holds the JUDGEMENT — which sources rot, what normal looks like — never the timestamps.
_bounded_by_design: ONE ROW PER POLL, overwritten in place. This is NOT an append-only run history, so the file size is bounded by the number of polls (~30 bytes/row) and cannot grow unbounded. `recent` keeps at most the last 3 results per poll as a rolling window for trend-spotting, and older results are dropped rather than archived — the durable trend lives in Ricky's memory.md, which is where judgement belongs. (Size Sally forecast, 2026-07-26: at one row per poll plus a 3-deep window, 20 polls lands around 4KB. Safe. An append-per-run design was rejected for exactly this reason.)
_row_shape: pollKey: { last_run: ISO-8601 or null · last_run_by: who stamped it · result: ok | no-change | incomplete | failed · note: one line, optional · recent: [{ run, result }] max 3 }
_due_math: A poll is DUE when now - last_run >= its registry cadence. last_run: null means NEVER RUN, which is due immediately and must be reported as 'never run' rather than as an overdue interval — an agent that renders `null` as a huge overdue number is lying with arithmetic.
